Assess Output Reproduction

Source: R/repro_indicators.R
assess_output_reproduction.Rd

Re-runs the submission's entry point in a fresh R session and checks that the outputs it produces match the submitted outputs. This is the executable counterpart to assess_clean_run_evidence(), which only checks that a run log is present. Returns evidence with indicator_id = "R-REPRO-008".

Usage

assess_output_reproduction(
  path,
  expected = NULL,
  entry = NULL,
  ctx = NULL,
  config = NULL,
  run = NULL,
  timeout = NULL
)

Arguments

path

Path to the submission's analysis code folder.

expected

Name of the subfolder, relative to path, holding the submitted outputs to reproduce. Defaults to config$expected_output_dir.

entry

Entry point script to run, relative to path. When NULL the first file matching config$entry_point_names is used.

ctx

A run context from r4subcore::r4sub_run_context(). When NULL a default context is created from the folder name.

config

A configuration from repro_config_default(). When NULL the default configuration is used.

run

Whether to execute the entry point. When NULL (default), execution happens only in an interactive session with 'callr' installed, so examples, tests, and CRAN do not run submission code unless asked.

timeout

Maximum seconds to allow the run. Defaults to config$run_timeout.

Value

A validated evidence table.

Details

Comparison separates analytical content from cosmetic bytes. Data outputs (CSV, text) must match byte for byte, but formatted outputs (rtf, pdf; see config$cosmetic_output_ext) embed a generation timestamp that changes on every run, so those are compared after the timestamps are stripped. An output that differs only in its embedded time still counts as reproduced, and the message says so; only a difference in the actual results is a failure.

Execution is opt-in and sandboxed. The folder is copied to a temporary location and the entry point runs in a separate R session (via 'callr') with a timeout, so nothing in the submission folder is modified. The submitted outputs under expected are hashed from the original folder and compared to the files the re-run produces in the copy. When run = FALSE, or 'callr' is not installed, no code runs and the indicator returns na, which keeps the check safe offline and on CRAN. When the outputs reproduce but the run happened on a non-Windows OS, the result is a warn, since FDA reviewers execute on Windows and the outputs must reproduce there.

Examples

d <- file.path(tempdir(), "sub008")
dir.create(file.path(d, "outputs"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
writeLines("writeLines('1', 'outputs/res.txt')", file.path(d, "run.R"))
writeLines("1", file.path(d, "outputs", "res.txt"))
ev <- suppressMessages(assess_output_reproduction(d, run = FALSE))
ev$result
#> [1] "na"
# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("callr", quietly = TRUE)) {
  ev2 <- suppressMessages(assess_output_reproduction(d, run = TRUE))
  ev2$result
}
#> [1] "warn"
# }
